title: World Book Day
strapline: Dress as your favourite character and step inside a story.
intent: A whole day given to books and stories tells children that reading is a joy worth celebrating.
Dressing as a favourite character deepens the bond with a story and sparks imaginative role-play.
Sharing their best-loved book grows children's sense of themselves as readers with real preferences.
Retelling, acting and talking about stories builds language, sequence and comprehension.
The day builds the love of books that underpins all later reading — chosen freely, for pleasure.
implementation: Invite children to come as a favourite character or bring a beloved book from home to share.
Fill the day with stories — read-alouds, acting out, story small-worlds — and let children choose the books.
Wonder together: 'Who have you come as? What happens in your story? Which part do you love best?'
Set up story corners and props so children can climb inside their favourite books and retell them.
Celebrate every child's choice equally — the well-thumbed board book matters as much as the long tale.
Follow the children — some will act out stories all day, others will curl up and pore over books.
key_questions: Who have you dressed up as today?
What is your favourite book — what happens in it?
Which part of the story do you love best?
What might happen next in this story?
Can you tell me your story in your own words?

impact.text: Children choose and share favourite books and show themselves as readers.
Children retell and act out stories with structure and detail.
Children dress as characters and sustain imaginative story play.
Children talk about stories — what happens, what might happen next.
Children build a rich bank of stories and love of books.

enhancements: A character dress-up day with a share-your-book table.
Story small-worlds and props for climbing inside favourite tales.
A cosy reading nook with a wide, tempting range of books.
A 'our favourite books' voting or display wall.
A story-acting stage with simple costumes and puppets.

playing_exploring: Children dress up, act out and lose themselves in favourite stories.
They explore a rich range of books and choose freely.
active_learning: Children stay deeply engaged with the books and stories they love.
They see a story retelling or act-out through to the end.
creating_thinking: Children imagine themselves as characters and invent what happens next.
They talk about why they love a story and what it means.
